reason: While the text does depict Yahweh as all-powerful (striking all the firstborn, granting favor to the Israelites, distinguishing between nations), it contradicts the characterization as 'remote.' The passage emphasizes direct, active divine engagement: Yahweh speaks directly to Moses (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה), gives detailed instructions, personally grants favor to the people in Egyptian eyes, and directly executes the tenth plague. This portrays an intimately involved God, not a remote one. The text shows Yahweh as immanent and interventionist rather than distant or uninvolved.
